If someone hurts you, you are allowed to "hate" them.

Also, I don't see how "freedom of speech" and "hate" are related.

Freedom of speech is your unbridled ability to say and do what you want,

I came here wanting to be a part of a community from it's early stages, and to get the user name that I wanted. Hatred is, in and of itself, a natural part of life. It drives people to do extraordinary things, whether they are good or bad. For example, some people have a hatred toward human suffering; they hate the fact that there are some people that cannot have a better quality of life just because they were not born "high enough" on the socioeconomic ladder. Others have a hatred toward groups of people (e.g. Nazi Germany). I feel that freedom of speech is an important factor necessary to build strong communities, but I also feel that each of those communities are in all of their right to restrict certain actions and behaviors for the sake of the weak, defenseless, an agreed-upon moral code, or some other perfectly justified reason. I'm not saying that what Pao is doing is right; she has her reasons (anti-bullying, money, you name it) and has the power to do so, so why not from her point of view. However, I don't like the consequences of her actions so that's why I'm exploring communities like this one for a calmer and more enjoyable experience. And for cute cat pictures.

Personally, my issue with Reddit was not that they got rid of FPH, but that they did so while proclaiming to be supporters of free speech. A private company has the right to do whatever it wishes with it's services, however it's the moral dissonance, and the inconsistent application of those morals that irked me.

I came here when I saw that reddit was no longer a place that was interested in defending controversial speech.

But to be honest I don't agree with you at all that hatred is unacceptable. Hatred is built into human nature. The urge to eliminate hatred will only provoke more hatred and make demonstrations of hatred more severe and more powerful. If anything, there should be MORE hatred in the world, not less.
